findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before assertion
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), the spawned reader thread runs `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` in a loop until `deletedAll` is observed true, but the main thread never calls `Thread.join()` (or otherwise awaits the reader) before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. Because the REST call is synchronous but can take nontrivial time, the reader thread may still be executing a `groups()` call when the main thread performs the assertion. As a result, an NPE thrown by the reader thread can land in `caughtExceptions` only after the assertion has already passed (or, conversely, the test can pass simply because the timing race was lost on this run). Without a join (or an explicit CountDownLatch/await), the assertion does not actually prove the bug is fixed. The thread should be joined, and `deletedAll` should be set after the join is set up so the reader can observe the latch, not the main thread.

findings.title: Null-guard added to getSubGroupsCount but not to other modelSupplier.get() call sites
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() was fixed to do `GroupModel model = modelSupplier.get(); return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` precisely because `modelSupplier.get()` (which delegates to `getGroupModel()` returning null when the underlying group is concurrently deleted) can produce a null. The same `modelSupplier.get()` is used unguarded in getSubGroupsStream(String,Integer,Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer) at line 268, all of the form `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. Under the same concurrent-deletion scenario these will still throw NPE. Either the fix should be applied consistently to all four methods, or `LazyModel` should be changed so that a null result is converted into a stable, non-NPE-throwing value (e.g., returning an empty stream) and the special case removed from each caller.

findings.title: Test does not exercise the path that NPE'd (getSubGroupsCount)
findings.body: The reader thread calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation=true`. The NPE fixed in this PR is in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(), which is only invoked from GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups when `subGroupsCount=true` (e.g., from the admin UI groups endpoint, not the default REST `groups` listing). If the brief-listing code path does not call getSubGroupsCount, the test will not actually reproduce the regression it claims to fix and the PR could pass CI while still shipping a broken getSubGroupsCount path. The test should either invoke the endpoint that calls populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups with subGroupsCount=true, or directly invoke getSubGroupsCount on a GroupAdapter that has been concurrently invalidated, so that a future regression in the fixed method is caught.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount can still throw IllegalStateException on concurrent deletion
findings.body: Even after the null-guard, `if (isUpdated()) return updated.getSubGroupsCount();` is reached only after isUpdated() itself. isUpdated() (lines 70-76) calls `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(...)` and throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` when `invalidated` is true but the group has been deleted. So the documented scenario (a group being accessed concurrently with its deletion) still produces an exception here, just a different one. If the goal of the fix is to make concurrent delete+read not throw, the null-guard should be at the top of the method (e.g., `GroupModel m = getGroupModel(); if (m == null) return null;`) and isUpdated()'s IllegalStateException should be downgraded or guarded, otherwise callers may continue to see exceptions and the test (which catches `Exception`) might still observe a failure via the related IllegalStateException rather than via the originally reported NPE.
